thread.title: Apple Stock Rises As iPhone Maker Expands In Austin And Five More Cities | Investor's Business Daily

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Apple Stock Rises As iPhone Maker Expands In Austin And Five More Cities | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) plans to spend $1 billion to expand its Austin, Texas, operations and establish new facilities in Seattle and San Diego, the iPhone maker said Thursday. Apple stock, meanwhile, rose although the Nasdaq again fell.
X The iPhone maker also plans to expand operations in Pittsburgh, Boulder, Colo., and Culver City, Calif., the company said. Pittsburgh has emerged as one hub for artificial intelligence research.
Contrary to reports, Apple's expansion plans apparently do not currently include North Carolina's Research Triangle Park area.
Apple's campus in Austin already has more than 6,000 employees. It started out there with technical support operations. But Apple later hired engineering staff to design chips for iPhones.
With the new $1 billion investment in Austin, Apple plans to add 5,000 employees right away. A new, 133-acre campus will enable Apple to house an additional 15,000 workers in the long run.

Apple Avoids Amazon-Like Bidding War "With this new expansion, we're redoubling our commitment to cultivating the high-tech sector and workforce nationwide," Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook said in a prepared statement.
Unlike Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple pursued its expansion plans without a bidding process. In the end, Apple opted to add operations in Austin rather than build a new, large facility. Amazon picked New York City and Northern Virginia outside Washington, D.C., for new corporate campuses.
Apple opened a new, $5 billion "spaceship" headquarters in Cupertino, Calif., in 2017. It's also expanding in nearby San Jose.
Apple stock gained 1.1% to close at 170.95 on the stock market today. Apple stock has slumped of late on worries that iPhone sales have peaked.
